searchAliases: Denver Public Schools family student calendar
districtFact: Denver Public Schools publishes family/student calendar PDFs that distinguish the first day for K-12 students from the first day for ECE students. DPS also marks conference/no-class days, vacation or staff-learning/no-class days, planning and professional learning days, other holidays and observances when school remains open, and a last day that is a half-day early release.

about.title: About Denver Public Schools Calendar Dates
about.content: This page summarizes districtwide dates from Denver Public Schools family/student calendar PDFs. Families should still check their school for bell schedules, athletics, testing, transportation notices, school-specific events, and any same-day updates from DPS.

planningTips.title: DPS Calendar Notes
content: DPS marks separate first days for K-12 and ECE students, so preschool families should not assume the K-12 start date applies.
The DPS calendar distinguishes holidays/no classes, conference/no classes, vacation or staff-learning/no classes, and other holidays and observances when school remains open.
The last day is marked as a half-day early release on the family/student calendars.

districtFaqs.q: Does Denver Public Schools use the same first day for ECE and K-12 students?
districtFaqs.a: DPS family and student calendars can mark separate first days for K-12 and Early Childhood Education students. Check the school-year page for the exact dates.

districtFaqs.q: Are all DPS holidays and observances no-school days?
districtFaqs.a: No. DPS separates holidays/no classes from other holidays and observances. The PDF notes that school is open on other holidays and observances unless the date is separately marked as no classes.

districtFaqs.q: Where should families verify DPS calendar updates?
districtFaqs.a: Use the official Denver Public Schools calendars page and school communications for final confirmation. MySchoolDates is an independent reference and is not affiliated with DPS.
